The Criminal Justice, Mental Health, and Substance Abuse (CJMHSA) Reinvestment Grant Program was created by section 394.656, Florida Statutes (F.S.), and is housed within the Department of Children and Families (Department). The purpose of this Request for Applications (RFA) is to provide funding under the Reinvestment Grant Program to counties which they may use to plan initiatives that increase public safety, avert increased spending on criminal and juvenile justice systems, and improve the accessibility and effectiveness of treatment services for adults and juveniles who have a mental illness, substance use disorder, or Co-Occurring mental health and substance use disorders, and who are in, or at-risk of entering, the criminal or juvenile justice systems. Pursuant to Line 355 of the General Appropriations Act (GAA), the CJMHSA Program has been extended to include veterans’ treatment court programs and training for 911 public safety telecommunicators and emergency medical technicians.

title: Patterson Loop 26/27 Timber Sale
agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services (FDACS)
description: MFMP MFMP for Vendors Vendor Disclosures State of Florida Advertisements Invitation to Bid Patterson Loop 26/27 Timber Sale Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services (FDACS) Advertisement Status: OPEN Last Edit Date/Time: 10/08/2026, 12:12 PM Advertisement Number: ITB-17186 Agency Advertisement Number: Version Number: 1 Published Date/Time: 10/08/2026 12:12 PM Start Date/Time: 10/08/2026 12:12 PM End Date/Time: 10/28/2026 02:00 PM Responses Open Date/Time: 10/28/2026 02:00 PM Commodity Codes Code Description 93141904 Agricultural or rural cooperatives services SALE ADVERTISEMENT Patterson Loop 26/27 Timber Sale The Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services, Florida Forest Service is seeking sealed bids for the sale of timber. Patterson Loop 26/27 Timber Sale in its entirety spans 254 acres. It is estimated to yield 1,427 tons of pine pulpwood/mulch wood and 165 tons of eucalyptus pulpwood/mulch wood. Broken down by species, this is a per unit sale thinning of approximately 220 acres of planted south Florida slash pine, and a clearcutting of approximately 34 acres of planted eucalyptus in Okaloacoochee Slough State Forest in Hendry County, Florida (see attached maps). These maps, and this project in general, divide the harvest into four separate areas referred to as Areas 1, 2, 3, and 4, corresponding to the stands proceeding West to East. The pine sale areas (Areas 1 and 4) are comprised of 19-23-year-old south Florida slash in the range of 200-400 trees per acre calculated through a range of 5-to-7-inch DBH. Timber available for harvest in Areas 1 and 4 include a 3rd row thinning with selection includes diseased, deformed, defective, forked, and suppressed trees. Both pine sale areas will have a target BA of 30 or higher post-harvest. The two smaller stands totaling 34 acres of planted eucalyptus plantations (Areas 2 and 3) were last clearcut 25 years ago. Areas 2 and 3 will be a clearcut. All areas will require low ground pressure equipment. Sale boundaries are roads, wetlands, fire lines or obvious timber type changes. This will be an eighteen (18) month contract. Interested parties may obtain complete bid information by contacting James Kavanagh at (239) 690-8031. The Florida Forest Service reserves the right to reject any and all bids and to waive any irregularity in bids received. Bids will be opened at: 10941 Palm Beach Blvd, Fort Myers, Fl 33905 10/28/2026 10:00 AM, EDT

The Sale Area is in Section 9; Township 11 South; Range 21 East. Sale boundaries include roads and firebreaks. (Maps are included in the attached agreement.) This timber salvage is due to an Ips beetle infestation. Harvest boundaries are categorized as either Primary or Optional. The Primary area is approximately 36.1 acres in size and designated for clearcut harvest of dead, dying, and green pine. The buyer is not obligated to harvest hardwood trees within this area. Within the Optional area, the buyer may cross the Primary boundary to harvest dead pine only; green pine is not available for harvest. The District’s Project Manager will determine the allowable extent of harvesting within the Optional area. All operations must commence within fourteen (14) calendar days of contract execution. The District estimates the volume of timber conveyed in this Agreement to be 860 tons of pine pulpwood, 126 tons of chip-n-saw, 1,550 tons of saw-timber, but there is no guarantee that the volume is present.

description: MFMP MFMP for Vendors Vendor Disclosures State of Florida Advertisements Invitation to Bid 224003 Chipley REVAMP Department of Military Affairs (DMA) Advertisement Status: OPEN Last Edit Date/Time: 10/21/2026, 07:06 PM Advertisement Number: ITB-17297 Agency Advertisement Number: Version Number: 3 Published Date/Time: 10/21/2026 06:51 PM Start Date/Time: 10/21/2026 08:00 PM End Date/Time: 12/17/2026 08:00 PM Responses Open Date/Time: 12/10/2026 07:00 PM Commodity Codes Code Description 72121100 Commercial and office building construction services 72121101 Commercial and office building new construction service 72121103 Commercial and office building renovation and repair service 72121400 Specialized public building construction services General Project Description (See Bid Documents for complete details): This is a full facility sustainment project that will address maintenance, repairs, and lifecycle replacement for buildings, building equipment and systems, utilities, and components of the 17,208 square foot Readiness Center and supporting assets to keep them in good working order. The intent is not to construct any new square footage, buildings, structures, etc., rather to sustain the overall asset inventory and maintain the asset inventory in good working order Roof repairs/roof replacements for buildings and structures. General maintenance/repair activities to exterior of buildings and structures to keep them in good working order. Seal building envelope(s) from the elements. General maintenance/repair activities in the Readiness Center and support building(s) functional areas outlined in NG PAM 415-12 (e.g. painting, flooring replacement, replace ceiling tiles as necessary, etc.). Repair/replacement of latrines/showers, fixtures, tile, flooring, lockers, etc. Repair/replacement of electrical systems/components. Repair/replacement of water systems and components (potable/non-potable, sewage, irrigation, fire suppression, etc.). Repair/replacement of HVAC systems/components. Repair/replacement of fire alarm system/components (alarm, mass notification system, fire suppression system, etc.). Repair/replacement of communications system/components as necessary. Repair/replace windows as necessary. Repair/replace fencing/gates as necessary, in order to maintain a secure facility. Repair/replace interior and exterior lighting as necessary. Parking Areas (MOV & POV) sealing/re-coating with asphalt (or similar) and re-striping parking spaces. Repair/replace Anti-Terrorism-Force Protection (ATFP) measures as necessary. Draining/grading work to address any site drainage/stormwater requirements as necessary. Repair/replace signage as necessary. Other sustainment work that is found to be necessary to keep the facility in good working order.

This is a salvage harvest of merchantable pine and hardwood timber that has been damaged by Hurricane Isaias on October 9, 2026, on Blackwater River State Forest in Santa Rosa County, Florida (SFI Certified Forest BVC-SFIFM-700005). Within the total area of 18,628 acres, Florida Forest Service staff have identified areas of extensive damage which may be identified on the attached maps and/or identified while harvesting is ongoing. Substantial damage areas will be the highest priority for harvesting and must be cut before lower damage areas. Approximately 1,727 acres surrounding red cockaded woodpecker clusters will also be prioritized and must be cut before March 15, 2027. The successful bidder must begin harvesting within 10 business days of contract execution. There is no volume estimate for this sale. Products include salvage pine pulpwood, salvage pine chip-n-saw, salvage pine sawtimber, and salvage hardwood pulpwood. All timber which is blown down, broken off, leaning more than 15 degrees, or otherwise damaged is available for harvest. Timber that does not meet these criteria may only be harvested by approval of the Forester-in-Charge. Sale boundaries will consist of roads, wetlands, forest boundaries, recreational sites, and any timber type changes or undamaged areas. This salvage is being advertised at the same time as the West Boundary 2026 Salvage Sale and Wolfe Creek 2026 Salvage Sale. In the event that the same bidder places the highest acceptable bid on multiple sales, the successful bidder must forfeit all but one sale to the next highest bidder to allow for a faster response or have adequate equipment and personnel to harvest multiple sales simultaneously. This will be a six (6) month contract. Interested parties may obtain complete bid information by contacting Eric Howell at (850) 957-5725. The Florida Forest Service reserves the right to reject any and all bids and to waive any irregularity in bids received. Bids will be opened at: 11650 Munson Highway, Milton, Fl 32570 10/29/2026 10:00 AM, CDT

title: Gulf to Lake 26/27 Timber Sale
agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services (FDACS)
description: MFMP MFMP for Vendors Vendor Disclosures State of Florida Advertisements Invitation to Bid Gulf to Lake 26/27 Timber Sale Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services (FDACS) Advertisement Status: OPEN Last Edit Date/Time: 10/23/2026, 02:12 PM Advertisement Number: ITB-17306 Agency Advertisement Number: Version Number: 1 Published Date/Time: 10/23/2026 02:12 PM Start Date/Time: 10/23/2026 02:12 PM End Date/Time: 11/12/2026 03:00 PM Commodity Codes Code Description 93141904 Agricultural or rural cooperatives services SALE ADVERTISEMENT Gulf to Lake 26/27 Timber Sale The Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services, Florida Forest Service is seeking sealed bids for the sale of timber. This sale is a clearcut of approximately 153 acres of sand pine from the Citrus Tract of Withlacoochee State Forest located in Citrus County, Florida (see attached maps). The sale area consists of natural and planted sand pine. Any longleaf pine that occurs within the sale boundary is not included in the sale and must not be harvested. Due to planned management activities, harvest boundaries are categorized as either Primary or Contingency. The Primary Area is approximately 138 acres in size. Timber available for harvest includes all sand pine timber within the Primary Area. The Contingency Area is approximately 15 acres in size. Harvesting in this area will only be approved if the timing of the harvest does not interfere with management activities (e.g. prescribed burning). Any harvesting in the Contingency Area will be at the direction of the Forester-in-Charge. The estimated volume for this sale is 7,347 tons of pine pulpwood/mulch wood. Of the total tons 6,627 tons are included in the Primary Area and 720 tons are included in the Contingency Area. The sale boundary is designated by distinct stand type change, roads, fire lines, and/or orange painted boundary trees. The length of this contract is for twelve (12) months. Interested parties may obtain complete bid information by contacting Genevieve Montgomery at (352) 382-0967. The Florida Forest Service reserves the right to reject any and all bids and to waive any irregularity in bids received. Bids will be opened at: 15019 Broad Street, Brooksville, Fl 34601 11/12/2026 10:00 AM, EST

title: Customer Service and Records Administration Services for ABLE United
description: MFMP MFMP for Vendors Vendor Disclosures State of Florida Advertisements Invitation to Negotiate Customer Service and Records Administration Services for ABLE United State Board of Administration (SBA) Advertisement Status: OPEN Last Edit Date/Time: 10/22/2026, 02:31 PM Advertisement Number: ITN-17045 Agency Advertisement Number: ITN26-01 Version Number: 2 Published Date/Time: 09/21/2026 08:30 PM Start Date/Time: 09/21/2026 09:00 PM End Date/Time: 05/31/2027 09:00 PM Responses Open Date/Time: 12/07/2026 07:00 PM Commodity Codes Code Description 80161500 Management support services The ABLE United Program requires comprehensive records administration, customer service, reporting, and operational support services necessary to operate a Qualified ABLE Program. The services summarized below and detailed further in the example Contract included as Appendix A, represent the minimum required services. The selected Respondent will provide these services in accordance with the Program disclosures (included as Appendix B) and the Business Rules (included as Appendix C). Respondents may propose additional enhancements that provide value to the Program. 3.01(1) Recordkeeping and Account Administration The selected Respondent will provide full-service recordkeeping and administrative support for ABLE Accounts, including account establishment and maintenance, processing of contributions and withdrawals, transaction recordkeeping, tax reporting, and other operational functions necessary to administer ABLE Accounts. The selected Respondent will also provide debit or prepaid card functionality for ABLE Account Owners as part of its core service offering. 3.01(2) Customer Service and Participant Support The selected Respondent will provide participant support services for ABLE Account Owners, contributors, and prospective participants across multiple contact channels, including telephone, online chat, electronic communications, and written correspondence. Respondents should be capable of supporting accessible communications and digital services consistent with ADA requirements. 3.01(3) Technology Platform and Online Access The selected Respondent will provide a secure, reliable, and scalable technology platform that enables online account opening and management, contribution and withdrawal processing, investment allocation changes, and participant access to account information and transaction history. The platform shall be accessible through web and mobile-compatible interfaces and designed to support a high-quality user experience consistent with accessibility standards, including compliance with applicable ADA requirements. The platform shall support integration with third-party systems, including financial institutions, payment processors, and Program partners, and shall maintain accuracy and consistency across systems. Security controls for the platform are addressed in Sections 3.01(6), 3.01(10, and 3.01(11). 3.01(4) Governance and Audit Support The selected Respondent will support Board oversight and Program administration through operational reporting and reconciliation support. The Respondent must maintain appropriate independent audit reports and provide documentation supporting operational controls and disaster recovery testing. 3.01(5) Data Ownership and Access The selected Respondent will maintain Program Data in a secure environment and acknowledges that all Program Data is owned by the Board. The Respondent shall provide the Board with timely, complete, and unrestricted access to Program Data for purposes including Program oversight, reporting, audit, and transition to a successor vendor. The selected Respondent shall maintain appropriate data access controls, audit logs, and data governance practices to ensure the integrity, security, and traceability of Program Data. The Respondent shall support data extraction and delivery in industry-standard, machine-readable formats upon request and shall ensure that 5 Program Data can be transferred to the Board or its designee without delay, degradation, or additional cost beyond agreed-upon contractual terms. 3.01(6) Data Protection and Security Controls The selected Respondent will maintain data protection and access controls appropriate for the administration of financial accounts and compliance with applicable federal and state requirements. The selected Respondent shall implement controls that include encryption of data at rest and in transit, user authentication, role-based access controls, and protection of sensitive information. Requirements for monitoring, fraud and threat detection, and incident response are addressed in Sections 3.01(8) and 3.01(10). Requirements for security governance, audits, reporting, and compliance documentation are addressed in Section 3.01(11). 3.01(7) Investment Option Administration The selected Respondent will support the administration of Board-approved Investment Options, including the allocation of contributions and withdrawals and coordination with underlying investment managers and custodians. The selected Respondent may also support the administration of an FDIC-insured option if approved by the Board. The selected Respondent must perform these services in compliance with applicable federal and state laws, regulations, and Program requirements governing Qualified ABLE Programs. 3.01(8) Incident Response and Cybersecurity Operations The selected Respondent will maintain a formal Incident Response Program to support the timely detection, response, and remediation of system and cybersecurity incidents. The selected Respondent shall develop and maintain a documented Incident Response Plan that defines roles, escalation procedures and communication protocols. The Plan shall be reviewed at least annually and updated as necessary. The selected Respondent shall notify the Board of any security breach as soon as practicable, participate in cybersecurity and disaster recovery tabletop exercises led by the Board, and shall coordinate with Board staff and other service providers during incident response activities. The selected Respondent shall document and report incidents, including preparing and delivering Root Cause Analysis (RCA) reports for critical and high-severity events, and shall demonstrate the ability to respond to and resolve incidents in a manner that minimizes impact to program operations and participants. 3.01(9) Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery The selected Respondent will maintain Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery (BC/DR) capabilities to ensure continuity of operations in the event of system disruptions or disasters. The Respondent shall develop and maintain a Business Continuity Plan that addresses operations within the first forty-eight (48) hours of a disruption and shall conduct annual testing of business continuity and disaster recovery plans. The Respondent shall identify and remediate any deficiencies. The Respondent shall monitor for fraud, suspicious activity, unauthorized access, and data anomalies. The Respondent shall implement automated alerting and escalation procedures and shall proactively identify, investigate, and resolve issues to maintain system stability and security. 3.01(11) Security Governance and Compliance The selected Respondent will maintain a comprehensive security and compliance program and a security governance framework aligned with applicable regulatory requirements and industry best practices. The Respondent shall conduct quarterly security audits and user access reviews and shall maintain audit logs for system access, data changes, and administrative activity. The selected Respondent shall participate in security training and awareness programs, including phishing simulations as required by the Board, and shall demonstrate compliance with applicable federal and state requirements governing financial accounts and data protection. title: Actuarial Services for the Stanley G. Tate Florida Prepaid College Program
description: MFMP MFMP for Vendors Vendor Disclosures State of Florida Advertisements Invitation to Negotiate Actuarial Services for the Stanley G. Tate Florida Prepaid College Program State Board of Administration (SBA) Advertisement Status: OPEN Last Edit Date/Time: 10/22/2026, 02:29 PM Advertisement Number: ITN-17258 Agency Advertisement Number: ITN 26-02 Version Number: 4 Published Date/Time: 10/14/2026 03:28 PM Start Date/Time: 10/14/2026 08:00 PM End Date/Time: 04/30/2027 12:00 PM Commodity Codes Code Description 80101512 Actuarial consulting services The Prepaid Plan requires independent actuarial analysis supporting the Board’s statutory duty to evaluate the actuarial soundness of the prepaid fund and to establish plan prices (See Appendix D for an overall description of the program). The services below are minimum requirements; the selected Respondent will perform them using data and assumptions supplied or approved by the Board and in accordance with applicable actuarial standards. 3.01(1) Transition Plan Submit and maintain an orderly transition plan, if applicable. The transition plan should describe the process, details, and schedule for providing an orderly transition from the current provider. The objectives of the transition plan should be to minimize the impacts on continuity of operations, maintain communication with staff, identify key issues, and overcome barriers to transition. 3.01(2) Annual Planning Meet in person with Board staff at least annually to plan the next 12 months of deliverables. As part of annual planning, review material Program experience, assumptions that may warrant further review, emerging actuarial issues, and potential analytical needs that may support significant Board policy, financial, or Program decisions. Provide a detailed annual work plan identifying Board data needs, delivery dates, review points, meetings, draft and final deliverables, and dependencies necessary to meet the Board’s schedule. 3.01(3) Data Review The Board will provide all data necessary to perform the specified contract services. Quarterly, the Actuary shall review, load, reconcile, and evaluate Board-provided data; investigate anomalies; determine whether information is complete and adequate; and recommend data improvements needed for valuations, pricing, and experience studies. (See Appendix I for an example data file). The selected Respondent shall protect Board data and use appropriate actuarial and statistical systems to perform and document all analyses. 3.01(4) Quarterly Actuarial Valuations and Cash Flows Prepare four quarterly actuarial valuation letters each year, as of June 30, September 30, December 31, and March 31, using the latest experience data, Board-approved assumptions, and anticipated future years of sales (as directed by the Board). Reports should include information, charts, breakdowns, and explanations in sufficient detail for the Board to understand the actuarial position of the Prepaid Plan. In addition, monthly undiscounted and discounted cash flows shall be provided to support the appropriate values in the report. See Appendix F for an example of a quarterly valuation report. 3.01(5) Annual Actuarial Valuation and Cash Flows Prepare one annual actuarial valuation report as of June 30. The report will update actuarial projections, include requested sensitivity analyses, reconcile surplus, review experience, recommend assumption changes when 4 appropriate, provide the program termination liability as provided for in Section 1009.98(8) Florida Statutes and with Board guidance, and provide projected undiscounted and discounted monthly cash flows. The Respondent shall review and analyze at least one major actuarial valuation assumption each year. See Appendix G for an example of an Annual Actuarial Adequacy Report NOTE: The annual actuarial adequacy review treats the Program as closed for valuation purposes, evaluating existing contracts without assuming any future sales. This approach does not mean the Program is closed to new purchases. Because the Program continues to sell plans each year, the quarterly actuarial reviews include estimated additional years of sales, as directed by the Board, and the associated future receipts and obligations. The resulting quarterly cash flow projections are used to construct the liability-driven investment (LDI) benchmark, aligning the investment strategy with projected net cash flows from both existing contracts and anticipated future sales. 3.01(6) Sensitivities Develop with the Board and periodically update a sensitivity matrix for material actuarial drivers. Where reasonably practicable, present the results in a form that helps staff understand the directional and approximate effect of defined changes on actuarial adequacy, projected cash flows, and plan pricing, together with appropriate limitations. 3.01(7) Annual Plan Pricing Prepare one annual Prepaid Plan pricing report each year for the designated enrollment period (currently July 1 through June 30), including plan prices by payment option and beneficiary age for each offered product. Test price adequacy, determine and disclose break-even rates of return, and provide illustrative prices at alternative inflation assumptions upon request. The Respondent shall review and analyze at least one major pricing assumption each year. See Appendix H for an example of the Annual Plan Pricing. 3.01(8) Supporting Files Provide electronic actuarial and pricing reports and usable supporting files, including payoff factors and projected cash flows, sufficient for Program operations, benchmark development, review of Board inputs and assumptions, and understanding of results. 3.01(9) Board Presentations and Consultation Appear before the Board annually, to explain and substantiate the annual actuarial adequacy and pricing reports. Consult with Board staff by letter, telephone, electronic communication, or in person upon request. 3.01(10) Professional Standards and Quality Control Perform all services in accordance with applicable qualification standards, Actuarial Standards of Practice, and the Actuarial Code of Professional Conduct. Maintain documented review and quality-control procedures for all deliverables. 3.01(11) Continuity Maintain a continuity plan, update it, and provide it to the Board annually, and cross-train personnel to preserve knowledge of the Prepaid Program. 5 3.01(12) Data Security and Confidentiality Maintain appropriate controls for confidential Board data, limit access to authorized personnel, use secure transmission and storage methods, and promptly report any incident affecting Board information. 3.01(13) Records, Documentation, and Audit Support Maintain work papers, models, assumptions, data reconciliations, and supporting documentation sufficient to reproduce and explain conclusions and to support Board oversight, audit, and transition to a successor provider. 3.01(14) Coordination and Responsiveness Coordinate with Board staff and other Board service providers, respond promptly to questions, identify emerging issues, and communicate any matter that may affect the accuracy, quality, or timeliness of deliverables. 3.01(15) Additional Actuarial Reports, Letters, or Assumption Studies At the Board’s request, conduct additional actuarial adequacy reports or letters, pricing reports or letters, or assumption studies. 3.01(16) Additional Actuarial Advisor Studies and Services At the Board’s request, and subject to advance written scope and fee approval, conduct additional sensitivity analyses, single-plan pricing analyses, or other special actuarial projects not identified above. 3.01(17) Workshops At the Board’s request, prepare and present an in-person workshop on calculations, data, assumptions, legislative changes, reporting, or improvements to models and methods. 3.01(18) Representation At the Board’s request, represent the Board before governing authorities on actuarial matters. 3.01(19) Legislation At the Board’s request, assist with preparation or review of legislation, fiscal notes, and bill analyses. 3.01(20) Other Value-Added Services Respondents may propose actuarial tools, dashboards, modeling enhancements, training, benchmarking, process improvements, or other services that provide additional value, efficiency, transparency, or risk reduction to the Board. Note: Illustrative annual adequacy, quarterly valuation, and pricing reports are informational and do not limit the Board’s ability to modify requirements during negotiations.

description: MFMP MFMP for Vendors Vendor Disclosures State of Florida Advertisements Invitation to Negotiate University of Florida - GradHaus University of Florida Advertisement Status: OPEN Last Edit Date/Time: 10/23/2026, 12:34 PM Advertisement Number: ITN-17296 Agency Advertisement Number: ITN2026-104 Version Number: 2 Published Date/Time: 10/22/2026 08:34 PM Start Date/Time: 10/22/2026 08:34 PM End Date/Time: 11/19/2026 10:00 PM Commodity Codes Code Description 80131500 Lease and rental of property or building Summary: The user of the proposed leased area is the University of Florida’s College of the Arts, GradHaus (Graduate Research in Art Development). All uses are for academic research and artistic practice in areas such as art + technology, ceramics, creative photography, drawing, painting, printmaking, and sculpture (students create artwork using a variety of materials) and related uses as necessary for operation. Tenant seeks a location to facilitate student art studios, collaboration, and meeting space. A roll-up loading door/dock with adequate access and parking. Access hours are generally Monday-Friday 8:00 a.m. - 5:00 p.m., but Tenant will need access after-hours and on weekends Additional Requirements and/or Limitations: The proposed Premises should include approximately 6,500-8,500 usable square feet to be reflected as rentable square feet for leasing purposes. The location desired is within a radius of 2 miles from the center of UF main campus and further defined in Exhibit “C” attached. Proposed locations outside of the defined area will be considered on a case-by-case basis. Delineation of space: The proposed premises should be relatively close to the general layout presented below. Square footages are estimates and dimensions do not have to be exact. Final space requirements may vary from the details below: Secured Area – A minimum of: • Concrete or other easy-care flooring. • 25 individual, open-to-structure, partitioned, design studio spaces of various sizes ranging from approximately 100 - 200 USF each. • 2 Administrative/advanced skill offices (approximately 180-250 USF each). • Graduate student open/lecture area to accommodate 8-10 students. Ideally the open spaces would be free of load bearing columns or walls that restrict movement or visual fields (approximately 1,000 USF). • Industrial sink and wash area with plumbing to accommodate use thereof. • Eye wash station. • 1 Break room/area (approximately 300-400 USF) with sink, cabinets, and room for a full-size refrigerator, table and microwave. • 1 Storage room (approximately 100-150 USF). • Parking spaces, user prefers at least 25 spaces with a minimum of 15 spaces (may be allocated and nonexclusive), approximately 4:1,000 SF. • 2 handicap accessible restroom(s) of adequate size to accommodate an office of this size. • Industrial level ventilation system. • Ability to store flammable materials in a Flammable Safety Cabinet. Timing: Occupancy is desired by May 1st, 2028.

description: MFMP MFMP for Vendors Vendor Disclosures State of Florida Advertisements Request for Information Healthy SNAP Evaluation Department of Children and Families (DCF) Advertisement Status: OPEN Last Edit Date/Time: 10/08/2026, 08:44 PM Advertisement Number: RFI-17189 Agency Advertisement Number: DCF RFI 2627 011 Version Number: 1 Published Date/Time: 10/08/2026 08:44 PM Start Date/Time: 10/08/2026 08:44 PM End Date/Time: 12/14/2026 10:00 PM Commodity Codes Code Description 85101700 Health administration services 85101701 Health policy 85101702 Health legislation or regulations 85101707 Health system evaluation services 85151505 Food research services 85151506 Studies on foods or food habits 85151604 Nutrition project evaluation The Department of Children and Families (Department), Office of Economic Self Sufficiency, is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to gather market intelligence from qualified vendors regarding available data sources, analytical capabilities, methodologies, and technology solutions for the analysis of Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) purchasing data. description: MFMP MFMP for Vendors Vendor Disclosures State of Florida Advertisements Request for Proposals Large- Capacity Central Plant Chillers Installation, Repair & Emergency Response Central Florida Tourism Oversight District Advertisement Status: OPEN Last Edit Date/Time: 10/08/2026, 06:36 PM Advertisement Number: RFP-17206 Agency Advertisement Number: RFP# C007152 Version Number: 1 Published Date/Time: 10/08/2026 06:36 PM Start Date/Time: 10/08/2026 06:36 PM End Date/Time: 10/29/2026 06:00 PM Commodity Codes Code Description 72101511 Air conditioning installation or maintenance or repair service 72151003 Heating system maintenance and repair service 72151200 Heating and cooling and air conditioning HVAC construction and maintenance services 72154102 Heat exchanger maintenance or repair service 72154110 Fin fan cooling tower maintenance and repair service 72154402 Pipefitting maintenance or repair service We are pleased to invite you to participate on Bid #C007152 . The following link is to our new bidding platform, hosted by PlanetBids™, where you can find the bid documents: BID LINK HERE. The District is seeking the assistance of experienced contractors to provide Large-Capacity commercial and industrial chillers, rated at 2,000 tons or more for installation, repair and emergency response for a three-year continuing contract term. Services will included at least twenty-six (26) chillers at five (5) different locations throughout the District. Typical items of work may include, but are not limited to chiller repairs, chiller cleaning, chiller removal, chiller motor installation, and industrial HVAC repairs. In addition, this contract shall serve to provide the District with emergency response for minor repairs.

This system accommodates multi-discipline services, including but not limited to Biology, Firearms, Chemistry and Toxicology. The current LIMS was acquired through competitive solicitation (RFP B1011) from Porter Lee Corporation in 2007 and is an essential element in maintaining FDLE Regional laboratories forensic accreditation standards. This system maintenance is critical to ensure that FDLE continues to meet business needs and national forensic laboratory standards.

title: Sunnyhill Restoration Area, West Tract 2027 Timber Sale
agency: St. Johns River Water Management Dist
description: MFMP MFMP for Vendors Vendor Disclosures State of Florida Advertisements Invitation to Bid Sunnyhill Restoration Area, West Tract 2027 Timber Sale St. Johns River Water Management Dist Advertisement Status: OPEN Last Edit Date/Time: 10/26/2026, 01:08 PM Advertisement Number: ITB-17322 Agency Advertisement Number: 42832 Version Number: 1 Published Date/Time: 10/26/2026 01:08 PM Start Date/Time: 10/26/2026 02:00 PM End Date/Time: 11/10/2026 07:00 PM Responses Open Date/Time: 11/10/2026 07:00 PM Commodity Codes Code Description 70151603 Timber production services 70151700 Forestry harvesting 72141504 Timber removal service The Governing Board of the St. Johns River Water Management District is requesting sealed bids for a per ton timber sale comprised of approximately 331.6 acres (“Sale Area”) within the Sunnyhill Restoration Area, located in Marion County, Florida. The Sale Area is in Section 12; Township 17 South; Range 24 East. Sale boundaries include roads, firebreaks, swamps, and obvious changes in timber type. (Maps are included in the attached agreement.) This timber sale includes marked timber and logger-select thinning. The marked area consists of 253.2 acres of mature slash pine, with harvest trees identified by blue paint at eye level. These trees were established approximately 38 years ago and thinned 16 years ago. The logger select area comprises 78.4 acres of mature slash pine to be thinned to a basal area of 40 to 45 square feet per acre. Stand 1902074A is optional for thinning. Although its overall density is already sufficiently low, the Purchaser may harvest poor-quality trees and thin dense pockets with prior approval from the District’s Project Manager. In logger-select areas, the thinning prescription is to first remove diseased, defective, and suppressed trees, then remove enough intermediate and codominant trees to achieve the desired density. The District estimates the volume of timber conveyed in this Agreement to be 3,815 tons of pine pulpwood, 1,775 tons of chip-n-saw, 1,178 tons of sawtimber, but there is no guarantee that the volume is present.
